pick.headline: Panama takes over the Canal Zone
pick.summary: On October 1, 1979, the Panama Canal treaties took effect: the Canal Zone ceased to exist and Panama assumed jurisdiction over the territory.
pick.significance: The handover began the twenty-year transfer of the canal under the Carter-Torrijos treaties, removing a long-standing grievance in US-Latin American relations.
pick.fbis: The Latin America Daily Report's October 1979 contents listed, under its Panama heading, continuing preparations for entry into the Canal Zone, a message from Royo, a planned diplomatic offensive and calls for a unified entry.

alternates.headline: Israeli jets bomb PLO headquarters in Tunis
alternates.summary: On October 1, 1985, Israeli aircraft bombed the PLO's headquarters at Hammam ash-Shatt near Tunis, killing some sixty people, in retaliation for the killing of three Israelis in Cyprus.
alternates.significance: The long-range raid on a friendly Arab state embarrassed Washington, which first called it legitimate and then abstained on a UN condemnation. Days later PLO gunmen seized the Achille Lauro.
alternates.fbis: The Middle East & South Asia contents for 1985 listed, under India, an item headed "New Delhi Condemns Israeli Raid on Tunisia", alongside Pakistani, Afghan and Iranian reporting.
